mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% does not lead to a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above a 5% year-over-year growth rate signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS YoY > 5% does not lead to a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a supply-side contraction, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO < 12-month MA does not lead to a statistically significant negative 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% year-over-year, the combination signals an accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%) does not lead to a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 per month signals strong labor market conditions, which historically correlates with increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases above 200,000 per month does not lead to a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST < 1 million does not lead to a statistically significant negative 5-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, the combination signals a weak economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the joint condition (INDPRO < 12-month MA and UNRATE > 7%) does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.
